author: nero_eth
content:
If we want to keep it being a subset of BiB, we'd use the same encoding, and would delay custody + sampling, and swapping out the merkle prove with kzg to a later point.
E.g. we should then keep the chunk size at 2048 bytes, have blobs be the data object and re-use `bytes_to_blobs` and `compute_cells`.

author: nero_eth
content:
Above you say blob and payload should be kept separate as they have different release times, as well as deadlines - I agree.
Similar applies to BALs: I think it's fine to encode them together but we shouldn't have both, BAL entries + txs  in one single blob. BAL and txs differ in their consumers, retention window and when they can be safely released, thus, by keeping them as separate groups over the blobs, we still allow BAL blobs to be released earlier without risking leaking txs at the same time.

author: .just_kk
content:
We will reuse some concepts introduced here such as segmenting the message into smaller chunks. However the exact scheme will be different. Execution payload broadcast is 1-to-many, whereas aggregations are N-to-many. 

We will include payload chunks merkle root commitment in the bid which will be then signed only once. That enables chunks verification by checking merkle path included in the message against the root. So we don't even need to include the signature in each chunk. 

For proofs propagation we don't have similar to bid concept. Each zk proof chunk will need to contain some form of signature from the aggregator

author: kevaundray
content:
> So we don't even need to include the signature in each chunk. 

this sounds right to me; given there's no slashing and verifying the merkle path is cheaper than verifying a pairing, the signature doesn't seem needed.

>  Each zk proof chunk will need to contain some form of signature from the aggregator
Ah okay, so in this case the aggregator doesn't send a signed root for the stark proof, they just keep sending signed chunks
